arguments.title: Basket quoting-engine specification and conformance suite
arguments.spec:
- Read the oracle (`candidates/conforming/index.mjs`) and the loose brief (`input/brief.md`) before writing anything; the oracle settles every threshold, rounding direction, and order of operations the brief leaves open.
- Deliverable A -- `spec/spec.json`: state all six rules R-01..R-06 as `{id, statement}` entries. Every statement must be at least thirty characters, must never simply repeat the brief's own loose sentence, and must pin down the exact threshold, rounding, and order of operations the oracle actually implements.
- Deliverable B -- `conformance/suite.mjs`: export `RULES` (every id declared in spec/spec.json) and `checkConformance(subject)` returning an array of `{rule, ok, detail}` with at least one entry per declared rule. The suite must never import anything from `candidates/` -- comparing against the oracle directly is a diff, not a conformance suite.
- The suite must accept the conforming (oracle) implementation on every declared rule -- a check the oracle cannot pass is wrong by definition.
- Only once every rule the brief names is stated AND checked may `spec/spec.json` set `"complete": true`; at that point the suite must also reject `candidates/nonconforming/` (it breaks exactly one rule -- the discount cap, R-03) and must reject a null implementation whose every export returns undefined.
- `input/`, everything under `test/`, and `scripts/run-tests.mjs` are frozen evidence -- never edit them; content digests are checked on every run.
- Acceptance for both deliverables is the same command: `npm test`, offline, no new dependencies.
